props.doc: Whether a week number column shows.

props.name: autofocus
props.doc: Whether the focused day takes focus when the calendar shows.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The calendar element.

DatePicker.doc:
A field-like button that shows a date, or a date range with `range`, and opens a
`Calendar` in a popover to change it. Enter, Space or Alt+Down opens the calendar, which
takes focus; a pick closes it. Bind `value`, or `rangeValue` in range mode.

props.name: value
props.doc: The picked date, in single mode.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with each picked date.

props.name: range
props.doc: Whether the picker picks a range.

props.name: rangeValue
props.doc: The picked range, in range mode.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.doc: Called with each picked range.

props.name: min
props.doc: The earliest date that can be picked.

props.name: max
props.doc: The latest date that can be picked.

props.name: isDateAllowed
props.doc: Decides which days within the limits can be picked.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: The text shown when nothing is picked. Defaults to the date format hint.

props.name: showWeekNumbers
props.doc: Whether the calendar shows week numbers.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The button element.

formatHexColor.doc: Formats `color` as `#RRGGBB`, or `#RRGGBBAA` when translucent and `withAlpha` is set.

parseHexColor.doc:
Parses `#RGB`, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`, with or without `#` and surrounding spaces;
returns `null` for anything else.

rgbToHsl.doc: Converts RGB to HSL; grays get hue 0.

rgbToHsv.doc: Converts RGB to HSV; grays get hue 0.

ColorFormat.doc: The text format of the color picker fields.

HslColor.doc: A color by hue (0 to 360), saturation, lightness and alpha (0 to 1).

HsvColor.doc: A color by hue (0 to 360), saturation, value and alpha (0 to 1).

RgbaColor.doc: A color with red, green, blue and alpha channels from 0 to 1.

ColorPicker.doc:
A color picker: a saturation and brightness area, a hue slider, an optional opacity
slider, text fields in a chosen format (hex, RGB or HSL) and optional `swatches`. Every
part works by pointer and keyboard: the arrows move the area and the sliders by 1%, or
10% with Shift, and the fields apply on Enter or when they lose focus. The color is
held as HSV, so a gray keeps its hue. Bind `value` (`#RRGGBB`, or `#RRGGBBAA` when
translucent). `ColorPickerButton` shows it in a popover.

props.name: value
props.doc: The color, as a hex string.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with each new color.

props.name: showAlpha
props.doc: Whether the opacity slider shows and the hex field keeps the alpha channel. Defaults to true.

props.name: swatches
props.doc: Preset colors offered below the fields, as hex strings.

props.name: defaultFormat
props.doc: The field format shown first. Defaults to `hex`.

props.name: width
props.doc: The picker width, in pixels. Defaults to 264.

ColorPickerButton.doc:
An outlined button with a color swatch and its hex value that opens a `ColorPicker` in a
popover. Bind `value`. `label` names the button and the popover, such as what the color
is for.

props.name: value
props.doc: The color, as a hex string.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with each new color.

props.name: showAlpha
props.doc: Whether the picker offers opacity. Defaults to true.

props.name: swatches
props.doc: Preset colors offered in the picker.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the button and the popover.

settleSnap.doc:
Returns the snap point closest to a bottom sheet dragged so its top sits `offset`
pixels below the tallest point, in a window `height` pixels tall, moved one step by a
fling (`velocity` in pixels per second toward the edge); `-1` dismisses it.

SheetSide.doc: The window edge a sheet slides in from; `start` and `end` follow the text direction.

Root.doc:
A panel that slides in from a window edge (`side`). A `modal` sheet dims the page and
keeps focus inside it; a click on the dimmed page closes it when `dismissible`. A
non-modal sheet leaves the page usable beside it. Either closes on Escape and, when
`dismissible`, when dragged toward its edge by its `Sheet.Handle`. A bottom sheet with
`snapPoints` (fractions of the window height, ascending) rests at those heights, and its
handle moves between them. Compose it with `Sheet.Trigger`, `Sheet.Content`,
`Sheet.Title`, `Sheet.Handle` and `Sheet.Close`.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the sheet is open.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Whether an uncontrolled sheet starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the sheet opens or closes.

props.name: side
props.doc: The edge the sheet slides in from. Defaults to `end`.

props.name: modal
props.doc: Whether the sheet dims the page and keeps focus. Defaults to true.

props.name: dismissible
props.doc: Whether a click outside and a drag toward the edge close it. Defaults to true.

props.name: snapPoints
props.doc: The heights a bottom sheet rests at, as fractions of the window height, ascending.

props.name: snap
props.doc: The index of the snap point the sheet rests at.

props.name: defaultSnap
props.doc: The snap point an uncontrolled sheet opens at. Defaults to 0.

props.name: onSnapChange
props.doc: Called when the sheet moves to another snap point.

props.name: children
props.doc: The trigger and the content.

Trigger.doc:
The button that opens a sheet: a `Button` (tonal by default) with the given props and
label.

props.name: variant
props.doc: The emphasis of the button. Defaults to `tonal`.

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon before the label.

props.name: children
props.doc: The label.

Content.doc:
The panel of a sheet, sliding in from its edge. A side sheet is `size` pixels wide; a
bottom sheet is as tall as its content up to 90% of the window, or rests at its snap
points. A modal sheet traps focus and dims the page; focus returns where it was when it
closes.

props.name: size
props.doc: The width of a side sheet, in pixels. Defaults to 360.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The panel element.

props.name: children
props.doc: The content.

Header.doc:
The header of a sheet: a `title`, `actions` and a close button, unless `closeButton` is
false. The title names the sheet for assistive technologies.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons at the end of the header.

props.name: closeButton
props.doc: Whether the header shows a close button. Defaults to true.

Body.doc: The scrolling body of a sheet, with large padding.

props.name: children
props.doc: The content.

Close.doc:
A button inside a sheet that closes it: a `Button` with the children as its label, or a
`CloseButton` without them.

props.name: variant
props.doc: The emphasis of a labeled button. Defaults to `text`.

props.name: children
props.doc: The label.

toast.doc: Shows a toast in the app's `Toaster` and returns its handle.

toaster.doc: The toasts the `toast()` functions show and the default `Toaster` renders.

ToasterStore.doc:
The toasts of an app: shown by `toast()`, rendered by `Toaster`. The toasts past
`maxVisible` wait their turn, and every timer pauses while the pointer is over the
toasts or focus is inside them.

Toast.doc: A short message shown by a `Toaster`.

ToastHandle.doc: Changes or closes a toast after it is shown.

ToasterPlacement.doc: Where a `Toaster` stacks its toasts; `start` and `end` follow the text direction.

Toaster.doc:
Shows the toasts of `toast()`: short messages in the inverse surface color, stacked at
`placement`, up to `maxVisible` at once (the rest wait). A toast closes after its
duration, by its close button or Escape, or by its action; the timers pause while the
pointer is over the toasts or focus is inside them. Screen readers hear each toast.
Place one `Toaster` inside the app's `ThemeProvider`.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Where the toasts stack. Defaults to `bottom`.

props.name: maxVisible
props.doc: How many toasts show at once. Defaults to 3.

props.name: maxWidth
props.doc: The largest toast width, in pixels. Defaults to 420.

props.name: store
props.doc: The toasts to render. Defaults to the ones of `toast()`.

FloatingPanel.doc:
A small window inside the app, such as a tool palette: a title bar with the desktop's
window controls over the content, placed at `rect` inside its positioned parent and kept
within it. Dragging the title bar moves it, the corner grip resizes it, the title bar
buttons minimize (to the bar), maximize (to the parent) and close it (`onClose`). With
focus on the panel itself, the arrows move it by `keyboardStep` and Shift+arrows resize
it. Bind `rect`.

props.name: title
props.doc: The panel title.

props.name: rect
props.doc: The panel's place and size.

props.name: onRectChange
props.doc: Called with the new rectangle while the panel moves or resizes.

props.name: minWidth
props.doc: The smallest size, in pixels. Defaults to 220 × 140.

props.name: minHeight
props.doc: The smallest height, in pixels. Defaults to 140.

props.name: resizable
props.doc: Whether the corner grip and Shift+arrows resize the panel. Defaults to true.

props.name: onClose
props.doc: Called by the close button; without it the panel has no close button.

props.name: controlStyle
props.doc: The style of the window controls. Defaults to `gnome`.

props.name: keyboardStep
props.doc: How far one arrow key press moves or resizes the panel, in pixels. Defaults to 16.

props.name: children
props.doc: The content.

TourController.doc: Runs a `Tour`: the steps, the current one and how it ended.

Tour.doc:
A guided tour of an interface, run by a `TourController`: the page dims except for a
spotlight on the current step's target, and a card next to it shows the step with Back,
Next (Done on the last step) and a skip button. The spotlight follows the target as the
page moves, and the target scrolls into view. Escape skips, the arrows go back and
forth. A step with `waitForTap` moves on when its target is clicked. Focus moves into
the card and returns where it was when the tour ends; `onFinish` tells whether it was
completed.

props.name: controller
props.doc: The tour to show.

props.name: onFinish
props.doc: Called when the tour ends, with whether every step was gone through.

ShortcutLabel.doc:
A keyboard shortcut drawn as key caps, in the platform's form: `Ctrl` `K` on Linux and
Windows, `⌘K` on macOS. Screen readers hear the shortcut as text. The platform comes
from the closest `SystemScope` unless `os` is given.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: The shortcut.

props.name: os
props.doc: The platform to label it for. Defaults to the system's.

ShortcutRecorder.doc:
A field that records a keyboard shortcut. A click, Enter or Space starts recording; the
next key with its modifiers becomes the shortcut (the platform's command modifier is
stored as the primary one, so it is `Ctrl` or `⌘` wherever it runs). Escape cancels,
Backspace or Delete clear it, and a button beside it clears it too. Bind `value`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The recorded shortcut, or `null`.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with each new shortcut, or `null` when cleared.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Whether the shortcut can't be changed.

props.name: os
props.doc: The platform to record and label for. Defaults to the system's.

rankCommands.doc:
Returns the commands that match `query`, best first: every word must appear in the
label, description, group or keywords (ignoring case and accents); labels that start
with the first word come first, then labels holding every word, then the rest, each in
their original order. Disabled commands never match.

CommandPalette.doc:
A searchable list of commands in a dialog near the top of the window: type to filter
(every word must match the label, description, group or keywords, ignoring case and
accents), Up and Down move the highlight, Enter runs it, Escape closes. Each row shows
the command's icon, label with the matches emphasized, group and description, and
shortcut. It lists `commands`, or the commands available where it is placed (its
`Commands` scopes). Bind `open`, or call `openCommandPalette()` for the palette without
an `open` prop.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the palette is open. Defaults to the state `openCommandPalette()` sets.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the palette opens or closes.

props.name: commands
props.doc: The commands to list. Defaults to the ones available where the palette is.

Root.doc:
A list of the items of `collection` that the user selects from, with the selection kept
in `controller` (or in a controller of its own, made from `mode` and `defaultValues`).

The list takes the focus as a whole and marks its active row. The arrow keys, Home and
End move the active row, which a single-selection list also selects. In a
multiple-selection list Space toggles the active row, Shift with the arrows extends the
selection and Control (Command on Apple platforms) with A selects all; clicks follow the
desktop conventions of `SelectionController.click`. Typing letters jumps to the next
matching label. Enter or a double click calls `onActivate`. Disabled items can't be
selected or activated.

Without children it renders every item, under its group heading when grouped, with
`item` as the content of each row, and `empty` when there are no items. Every row is
rendered, so it suits lists of up to a few hundred items; use `TreeView` for more.

props.name: collection
props.doc: The items.

props.name: controller
props.doc: The selection over `collection`; the list keeps its own when left out.

props.name: mode
props.doc: How many items the list's own controller selects. Defaults to `single`.

props.name: defaultValues
props.doc: The values the list's own controller selects at first.

props.name: onValuesChange
props.doc: Called with the selected values, in collection order, whenever they change.

props.name: onActivate
props.doc: Called on Enter or a double click on an enabled item.

props.name: item
props.doc: The content of a row of the default rendering, given the item and whether it is selected.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What the default rendering shows when there are no items.

props.name: children
props.doc: The parts: `ListBox.Item`, `ListBox.Group`, `ListBox.Empty`.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

Item.doc:
A row of a list box, identified by `value` in the list's collection. A click selects it
with the desktop conventions and a double click calls the list's `onActivate`. The
children replace `label`; a multiple-selection list adds a check mark to selected rows.

props.name: value
props.doc: The value of the item in the collection.

props.name: label
props.doc: The text shown when there are no children.

props.name: children
props.doc: Custom content.

Group.doc:
A group of list box rows under a heading: `label`, or a `ListBox.GroupLabel` among the
children.

props.name: label
props.doc: The heading.

props.name: children
props.doc: The rows, and a `ListBox.GroupLabel` when there is no `label`.

GroupLabel.doc: The heading of a `ListBox.Group`, which names the group for assistive technologies.

props.name: children
props.doc: The heading text.

Empty.doc: What a list box shows when its collection has no items; rendered only then.

props.name: children
props.doc: The content.

ListBoxState.doc:
The state a `ListBox.Root` shares with its parts: the active row, which the arrow keys
move, and the selection gestures of the keyboard and the pointer.

TreeController.doc:
The open, selected and checked nodes of a `TreeView`, by node value.

Its state is reactive: reading it in a template or `$derived` tracks it. Each set is an
immutable snapshot that the controller replaces when it changes.

treeCheckStates.doc:
Returns the check state of every node of `collection` in one pass: a leaf is checked when
`checked` has it, a branch is checked when all of its leaves are, unchecked when none are
or it has no leaves, and `mixed` otherwise.

TreeCheckState.doc: The check state of a tree node: checked, unchecked, or `mixed` when only some of a branch's leaves are checked.

TreeView.doc:
A tree of the nodes of `collection`, with the open, selected and checked nodes kept in
`controller`.

Only the rows in view are rendered, so it handles large trees; give it a height. The tree
takes the focus as a whole and marks its active row:

- Up, Down, Home and End move the active row; a single-selection tree selects it, and
  Shift extends a multiple selection.
- Right opens a branch or moves to its first child; Left closes it or moves to the parent
  (swapped in right-to-left layouts).
- Space toggles the check box of a `checkable` tree, or else the selection of a
  multiple-selection one; Control+A (Command+A) selects every shown, enabled node of a
  multiple-selection tree.
- Enter, or a double click, calls `onActivate`, or opens or closes a branch when it is
  not set.
- F2 starts an inline rename of the active node when `onRename` is set; Enter or leaving
  the field confirms it and Escape cancels it.
- Typing letters jumps to the next shown label that starts with them.

A branch with no children yet and an `onLoadChildren` shows a spinner while its children
load the first time it opens. A non-empty `query` shows only the matching nodes and their
ancestors, all open, with the match highlighted; branches can't be opened or closed while
filtering.

props.name: collection
props.doc: The nodes of the tree.

props.name: controller
props.doc: The open, selected and checked nodes; the tree keeps its own when left out.

props.name: item
props.doc: The content of a row after its disclosure, check box and icon; the label by default.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon before the label, given the node and whether it is open.

props.name: onActivate
props.doc: Called on Enter or a double click on a node; when not set, those open or close a branch.

props.name: onLoadChildren
props.doc:
Loads the children of an empty branch the first time it opens; the app adds them to
`collection`. When the promise rejects, the branch closes, `onLoadError` is called
(the error is logged when it isn't set) and opening the branch again retries.

props.name: onLoadError
props.doc: Called when `onLoadChildren` rejects.

props.name: onRename
props.doc:
Called with a node and its new, trimmed label when a rename is confirmed with a
non-empty label that differs from the old one; F2 renames nothing when not set.

props.name: checkable
props.doc: Whether the rows have tristate check boxes, tracked in `controller.checked`.

props.name: query
props.doc: The text that filters the nodes; blank shows the whole tree.

props.name: rowHeight
props.doc: The row height in pixels; defaults to the control height of the density.

props.name: indent
props.doc: The indent of each level in pixels. Defaults to 16.

props.name: overscan
props.doc: The rows rendered beyond each edge of the view. Defaults to 8.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

jsonTree.doc:
Returns the tree of decoded JSON `data`: objects and arrays become branches, other values
leaves, and the top node is labeled `rootLabel`. Node values are JSON paths, such as
`$.items[0].name`.

jsonValueText.doc: Returns `value` as JSON text, or its plain text when JSON can't encode it.

JsonEntry.doc: A key and value of a node of a `JsonTreeView`.

JsonTreeView.doc:
A tree view of decoded JSON `data`, with keys, strings, numbers, booleans and null in the
theme's syntax colors, and the size of each object and array.

Branches up to `expandDepth` levels deep start open, and open to it again when `data`,
`rootLabel` or `expandDepth` change. It has the keyboard and filtering of `TreeView`;
`query` filters by key and value. Give it a height.

props.name: data
props.doc: The decoded JSON: objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null.

props.name: expandDepth
props.doc: The depth up to which branches start open; 0 keeps every branch closed. Defaults to 1.

props.name: rootLabel
props.doc: The label of the top node. Defaults to `root`.

props.name: query
props.doc: The text that filters the nodes.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

avatarColor.doc:
Returns the accent color an avatar without a picture uses for `name`, picked by a stable
hash of its UTF-16 code units, or `null` when `name` is blank.

initials.doc:
Returns the initials of `name`: the first letters of its first and last words, in upper
case, or an empty string when `name` is blank. A letter is a whole user-perceived
character, so decomposed accents and emoji sequences stay intact.

AvatarShape.doc: The outline of an `Avatar`: a circle or a rounded square.

AvatarStatus.doc: A presence status shown as a dot on an `Avatar`.

Avatar.doc:
A picture of a person or thing: `src` when it loads, otherwise the initials of `name` on
a color picked from the name, otherwise `icon`.

The initials show while the image loads and if it fails. A `status` adds a presence dot
at the bottom end. Assistive technologies read `name` and the status as one image.

props.name: src
props.doc: The URL of the picture shown once it loads, over the initials or icon.

props.name: name
props.doc: The name the initials, the color and the accessible name come from.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon shown when `name` is blank. Defaults to a person.

props.name: size
props.doc: The width and height in pixels. Defaults to 40.

props.name: shape
props.doc: The outline. Defaults to `circle`.

props.name: status
props.doc: The presence status, shown as a dot.

props.name: background
props.doc: The background behind the initials or icon; defaults to a color picked from `name`.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name; defaults to `name` and the status. Without either the avatar is decorative.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

AvatarGroup.doc:
A row of overlapping avatars, showing at most `max` and a "+N" bubble for the rest. The
ring around each avatar and the bubble follow `shape`.

props.name: avatars
props.doc: The avatars.

props.name: max
props.doc: The number of avatars shown before the "+N" bubble. Defaults to 4.

props.name: size
props.doc: The avatar size in pixels. Defaults to 32.

props.name: overlap
props.doc: The fraction of each avatar the next one covers, from 0 up to, but not including, 1. Defaults to 0.3.

props.name: shape
props.doc: The shape of the avatars. Defaults to `circle`.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the whole group, such as "Project members".

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

Marquee.doc:
Scrolls its content continuously when it is longer than the space it has, such as a news
ticker or a long song title.

The content moves toward the reading start (up when vertical), or the other way with
`reverse`, at `speed` pixels per second, followed by a copy after `gap`. It stops while
the pointer or the focus is on it, and stays still at its start when the user prefers
reduced motion. `fadeEdges` fades the content at both ends. Content that fits doesn't
move. Assistive technologies read the content once; the copy is hidden and inert, so
plain content, such as text or icons, fits best. A vertical marquee needs a height.

props.name: children
props.doc: The scrolling content.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: The direction of the scroll. Defaults to `horizontal`.

props.name: reverse
props.doc: Whether the content moves toward the reading end (down when vertical).

props.name: speed
props.doc: The speed in pixels per second. Defaults to 40.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between the content and its copy, in pixels. Defaults to 32.

props.name: pauseOnHover
props.doc: Whether the pointer or the focus stops the scroll. Defaults to true.

props.name: fadeEdges
props.doc: Whether the content fades at both ends while it scrolls. Defaults to true.

props.name: fadeExtent
props.doc: The length of the fades in pixels. Defaults to 24.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

formatDuration.doc:
Formats `milliseconds` as `m:ss`, or `h:mm:ss` from an hour, with tenths of a second
(truncated) when `tenths` is set. A negative duration gets a leading minus sign.

TimerController.doc:
A stopwatch, or a countdown when `countdown` is set, that ticks every `interval` while
it runs.

Its state is reactive: reading `elapsed`, `remaining`, `isRunning` or `isCompleted` in a
template or `$derived` updates on every tick. A countdown stops by itself at zero and
calls `onComplete`. Time is measured from the clock, so it stays exact however late the
ticks arrive. Call `dispose()` when the timer is no longer used.

TimerText.doc:
The time of a `TimerController` as text: the remaining time of a countdown or the elapsed
time of a stopwatch, in tabular figures so the digits don't shift.

props.name: controller
props.doc: The timer shown.

props.name: tenths
props.doc: Whether tenths of a second show; without them a countdown rounds up to the whole second.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

animatedIcons.doc:
The animated icons of @oito2/ui, drawn on a 24-pixel grid in the stroke style of the
Lucide icons. The `Filled` variants cut their inner mark out of the fill, so the
background shows through it.

AnimatedIconData.doc:
The drawing and timing of an animated icon, such as `animatedIcons.ok`.

`frame` returns the SVG elements of the frame at `progress`, from 0 to 1, on a 24 × 24
grid in `currentColor`; `id` is unique to the icon instance and prefixes the ids of the
masks and clip paths the frame defines.

IconShape.doc: An SVG element of an animated icon frame, with its attributes and children.

AnimatedIconName.doc: The name of an icon of `animatedIcons`.

AnimationMode.doc: How an `AnimatedIcon` plays: once when shown or changed, over and over, or not at all (the final frame).

AnimatedIcon.doc:
An animated icon, such as `animatedIcons.ok`, drawn in SVG.

It plays according to `mode`, at `size` (the icon size of the density by default) in
`color` (the text color by default). When the user prefers reduced motion it shows the
final frame. Without a `label` it is hidden from assistive technologies, as a decorative
icon.

props.name: data
props.doc: The drawing and timing of the icon.

props.name: mode
props.doc: How the animation plays. Defaults to `once`.

props.name: size
props.doc: The width and height in pixels; defaults to the icon size of the density.

props.name: color
props.doc: The color; defaults to the text color.

props.name: duration
props.doc: The length of one play in milliseconds; defaults to the data's duration.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name; when left out the icon is decorative.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

PlaceholderIcon.doc:
A decorative square that stands in for a missing picture, such as an album cover or an
app icon that has not loaded: a rounded square in a container tone with a picture
outline in its center. It is hidden from assistive technologies.

props.name: size
props.doc: The width and height in pixels. Defaults to 48.

props.name: radius
props.doc: The corner radius: a radius token (`small`, `medium`, `large`) or a number of pixels. Defaults to `medium`.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

DiagonalClip.doc:
Clips its content along a diagonal, keeping the triangle on the side of `corner`. Place
two of them on top of each other to split an area diagonally, for example to preview
light and dark themes in one swatch.

props.name: corner
props.doc: The corner whose triangle is kept, cut by the diagonal between its two neighbors.

props.name: children
props.doc: The clipped content.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

defaultLanguages.doc:
The languages a `Highlighter` registers by default, keyed by name: the same 27 as
oito2_ui. highlight.js ships about 190 more grammars under
`highlight.js/lib/languages/`; pass them to a `Highlighter` to add them. Only the
grammars imported end up in the app.

HighlighterTheme.doc: Builds highlight.js scope styles from a syntax palette.

roleOfScope.doc: Returns the palette role of the highlight.js `scope`, or `foreground` for plain text and unlisted scopes.

scopeRoles.doc:
The palette role of every highlight.js scope the highlighter colors, such as `keyword`,
`title.function` or `selector-tag`. Scopes not listed render in the foreground color.

ScopeStyle.doc: The style of a highlight.js scope: its color, and italics or bold.

Highlighter.doc:
Splits source code into runs colored with the roles of a syntax palette, through
highlight.js grammars. Tokenizing runs synchronously in JavaScript, with no native code.

```ts
const { runs } = Highlighter.instance.highlight('let x = 1', { language: 'ts' });
```

HighlightedCode.doc: Code split into colored runs by a `Highlighter`.

SyntaxRun.doc: A run of highlighted code: text that shares one token scope and role.

CodeBlock.doc:
A read-only block of highlighted code on the container surface, with optional line
numbers and a copy button. The text can be selected; long lines scroll horizontally
instead of wrapping, and the scrolling area takes the keyboard focus so the arrow keys
scroll it.

The colors come from the `--oito2-syntax-*` roles of the enclosing `ThemeProvider`. The
code uses JetBrains Mono when the app imports `@oito2/ui-syntax/fonts.css`, and the
system monospace fonts otherwise.

props.name: code
props.doc: The source code.

props.name: language
props.doc: The language name or alias, such as `ts`; missing or unregistered shows plain text.

props.name: autoDetect
props.doc: Whether a missing `language` is guessed among the registered ones.

props.name: highlighter
props.doc: The highlighter; defaults to `Highlighter.instance`.

props.name: showLineNumbers
props.doc: Whether line numbers show.

props.name: showCopyButton
props.doc: Whether the copy button shows. Defaults to true.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the code area, such as the file name.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

qrErrorLevels.doc: The error levels, from the least to the most error correction.

qrModules.doc:
Returns the dark modules of the QR code of `data` in the smallest version that holds it
at `errorLevel`, choosing the encoding as oito2_ui does: digits only in numeric mode,
upper-case letters, digits and ` $%*+-./:` in alphanumeric mode, and anything else as
UTF-8 bytes. Throws a `RangeError` when `data` doesn't fit in a QR code at that level.

qrPath.doc:
Returns the SVG path data of the dark modules of `qr` on a grid of one unit per module,
offset by the quiet zone, leaving out the modules under a centered square `hole` (a
fraction of the module area's width, 0 for none). With `rounded` the modules are rounded
squares; otherwise squares, slightly enlarged to hide hairline seams.

qrQuietZone.doc: The width of the quiet zone around a QR code, in modules.

QrErrorLevel.doc:
How much of a QR code can be damaged or covered and still read, as error correction data
takes more room: about 7% (`low`), 15% (`medium`), 25% (`quartile`) or 30% (`high`).

QrModules.doc: The dark modules of a QR code, as a square grid.

QrCode.doc:
A QR code of `data` in SVG, painted in `color` on `background` with the standard
four-module quiet zone.

The defaults are black on white, which every scanner reads; custom colors need strong
contrast, with `color` darker than `background`. A `centerImage`, such as a logo, covers
the middle of the modules; the error level is then `high`, which recovers the most
covered modules, so the code still reads. When `data` doesn't fit, `error` or a localized
message shows instead.

props.name: data
props.doc: The encoded text, such as a link.

props.name: size
props.doc: The width and height in pixels, quiet zone included. Defaults to 160.

props.name: errorLevel
props.doc: The error correction level; ignored with `centerImage`, which uses `high`. Defaults to `medium`.

props.name: color
props.doc: The dark module color. Defaults to black.

props.name: background
props.doc: The light module and quiet zone color. Defaults to white.

props.name: rounded
props.doc: Whether dark modules are drawn as rounded squares.

props.name: centerImage
props.doc: The URL of an image drawn in the middle, such as a logo.

props.name: centerImageFraction
props.doc: The share of the module area's width cleared for the center image, above 0 and up to 0.3. Defaults to 0.22.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name; defaults to the localized "QR code".

props.name: error
props.doc: What shows when `data` doesn't fit in a QR code.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

SignatureController.doc:
The strokes of a `SignaturePad`, with undo, clear and export.

Its state is reactive: reading `strokes` or `isEmpty` in a template or `$derived` updates
as the user draws. Positions are in the pad's pixels; `size` is the pad size the strokes
were drawn in, which the exports use.

paintStrokes.doc:
Paints `strokes` in `color` on `context`: round dots for single points, and segments whose
width moves from one point's width to the next.

SignatureImageOptions.doc: The options of the raster exports of a `SignatureController`.

SignaturePoint.doc: A point of a signature stroke, in the pad's pixels, with the stroke width there.

SignaturePad.doc:
An area to sign with a mouse, finger or pen.

Strokes get thinner as the pointer moves faster, between `minWidth` and `maxWidth`, like
ink, and a pen's pressure makes them wider. With `showActions`, undo and clear buttons sit
in a corner. Assistive technologies hear whether the pad is empty or signed.

props.name: controller
props.doc: The controller that holds the drawn strokes.

props.name: height
props.doc: The pad height in pixels; it takes the available width. Defaults to 180.

props.name: color
props.doc: The ink color, as a CSS color; defaults to the text color.

props.name: minWidth
props.doc: The thinnest stroke in pixels. Defaults to 1.2.

props.name: maxWidth
props.doc: The thickest stroke in pixels. Defaults to 3.6.

props.name: showActions
props.doc: Whether undo and clear buttons show. Defaults to true.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: The text shown on the empty pad; defaults to the localized "Sign here".

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name; defaults to the localized "Signature".

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

CropController.doc:
The zoom, pan, rotation and flip of an `ImageCropper`, and the crop itself.

Its state is reactive. The pan is in the crop box's pixels and is kept so the image
always covers the box.

loadCropImage.doc:
Loads the image at `src` and, when its longest side is above `maxDimension`, scales it
down onto a canvas, keeping its aspect ratio, to bound the memory it takes.

CropImage.doc: An image a `CropController` can draw: a loaded image, a canvas or a bitmap.

CropOffset.doc: A pan in the crop box's pixels.

ImageCropper.doc:
Crops the image at `src`: the user zooms and pans it under a crop box of `aspectRatio`,
rotates it by quarter turns and flips it, and the app reads the result from `controller`.

The image moves by dragging and zooms by pinching, the mouse wheel or the toolbar. With
the focus on the crop area the arrow keys pan (more with Shift), plus and minus zoom, R
rotates (Shift+R the other way) and H flips. With `circle` the box is a circle.
`CropPreview` shows the result live.

props.name: src
props.doc: The URL of the image to crop, such as an object URL of a picked file.

props.name: controller
props.doc: The controller that holds the zoom, pan, rotation and flip.

props.name: aspectRatio
props.doc: The crop box width divided by its height; ignored with `circle`, which uses 1. Defaults to 1.

props.name: circle
props.doc: Whether the crop box is a circle.

props.name: height
props.doc: The height of the crop area in pixels. Defaults to 320.

props.name: showToolbar
props.doc: Whether the zoom, rotate, flip and reset controls show. Defaults to true.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the crop area; defaults to the localized "Image cropper".

props.name: maxDecodedDimension
props.doc:
The longest side, in pixels, the image is kept at; larger images are scaled down,
keeping their aspect ratio, to bound the memory they take. `null` keeps the full
size. Defaults to 4096.

props.name: onError
props.doc: Called when the image fails to load; the error is logged when it isn't set.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

CropPreview.doc:
The current crop of a `CropController` at `width`, updated as the user zooms, pans,
rotates and flips. It is hidden from assistive technologies.

props.name: controller
props.doc: The controller whose crop is shown.

props.name: width
props.doc: The preview width in pixels; the height follows the crop box. Defaults to 96.

props.name: circle
props.doc: Whether the preview is cut to a circle.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

NavigationMenuState.doc:
The state a `NavigationMenu.Root` shares with its parts: the open panel, whether it was
opened from the keyboard, the hover timers and the item elements the indicator follows.

Root.doc:
A website-style header menu: links and triggers in a row (`NavigationMenu.List` of
`NavigationMenu.Item`s), a line that slides under the `current` item
(`NavigationMenu.Indicator`) and flyout panels below the triggers
(`NavigationMenu.Content`).

A panel opens on hover after `hoverDelay`, or when its trigger is clicked or gets the Down
arrow, which also move the focus into it; moving the pointer to another trigger switches
panels at once. Tab moves between the items and Escape closes a panel. Bind `value` for
the open item.

props.name: value
props.doc: The value of the item whose panel is open, or `null`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The open item of an uncontrolled menu at first. Defaults to none.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called when the open item changes.

props.name: current
props.doc: The value of the item that marks the current page.

props.name: hoverDelay
props.doc: The wait in milliseconds before a hovered trigger opens its panel. Defaults to 150.

props.name: panelMaxWidth
props.doc: The largest panel width in pixels. Defaults to 560.

props.name: children
props.doc: The list and the indicator.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

List.doc: The row of items of a navigation menu.

props.name: children
props.doc: The `NavigationMenu.Item`s.

Item.doc:
An entry of a navigation menu, identified by `value`: a `NavigationMenu.Link`, or a
`NavigationMenu.Trigger` with its `NavigationMenu.Content`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The value of the item, unique in the menu.

props.name: children
props.doc: A link, or a trigger and its content.

Trigger.doc:
The button of a navigation menu item that opens its `NavigationMenu.Content`: on hover,
on a click or on the Down arrow, the last two moving the focus into the panel.

props.name: children
props.doc: The label.

Link.doc:
A navigation menu item that goes somewhere: a link to `href`, marked as the current page
when its item is the menu's `current` one.

props.name: children
props.doc: The label.

Content.doc:
The flyout panel of a navigation menu item, below its trigger. It stays open while the
pointer is over it, and takes the focus when it was opened from the keyboard or a click.

props.name: children
props.doc: The panel content, such as a grid of links.

Indicator.doc:
The line that slides under the `current` item of a navigation menu; place it inside
`NavigationMenu.Root`, next to the list. It is hidden from assistive technologies.

acceptAttribute.doc: Returns the `accept` attribute of a file input for `groups`: their extensions with a dot and their MIME types.

baseName.doc: Returns the last segment of `path`, split at `/` or ``.

extensionOf.doc: Returns the lower-case extension of `name` without the dot, or `null` when it has none.

fileMatchesTypes.doc:
Whether `file` is one of the `accept`ed types: no groups, or a group without extensions
and MIME types, accept every file.

isPreviewableImage.doc: Whether `file` is an image a browser shows, by MIME type or extension; SVG files are left out.

mimeTypeOf.doc: Returns the MIME type of a common file extension in `name`, or `null`.

webFile.doc: Returns a `PickedFile` for a browser `file`; `isDirectory` marks a dropped folder.

FileTypeGroup.doc:
A group of accepted file types, such as "Images": files whose name ends with one of
`extensions` (with or without the dot, in any letter case) or whose MIME type is one of
`mimeTypes`, where `image/*` matches every image type. A group with neither accepts
every file.

PickedFile.doc:
A file the user chose or dropped: a browser `File` on the web, a path on the file system
in Tauri. Its size and content are read on demand.

FileUploadController.doc:
The files of a file upload, checked against the `accept`ed types, `maxFileSize` and
`maxFiles` as they are added; directories are always refused.

Its state is reactive. `add` keeps the files that pass the checks and lists the others in
`rejected`, which holds the refusals of the last `add` only.

FileRejection.doc: Why a `FileUploadController` refused a file: its type, its size, the file count, or because it is a directory.

RejectedFile.doc: A file a `FileUploadController` refused, with the reason.

defaultFilesAdapter.doc: Returns the adapter of the platform: `tauriFilesAdapter` inside Tauri, `webFilesAdapter` in a browser.

DropTargetHandlers.doc: The handlers of a drop target: whether files are dragged over it, and the files dropped.

FilesAdapter.doc:
How the file components reach the platform: the file chooser, the "Save as" flow and
files dropped from the desktop. `webFilesAdapter` uses the browser and
`tauriFilesAdapter` the Tauri dialog and fs plugins.

webFilesAdapter.doc:
Returns the browser adapter: an `<input type="file">` for the file chooser, HTML drag and
drop for dropped files (folders marked as directories) and a `Blob` link with `download`
for saving, which always reports the file as saved.

dialogFilters.doc: Returns the dialog filters of `groups`: one per group with extensions, named by its label or extensions.

pathFile.doc: Returns a `PickedFile` for the file system `path`; `isDirectory` marks a folder.

tauriFilesAdapter.doc:
Returns the Tauri adapter: the file chooser and "Save as" dialogs of the dialog plugin,
file sizes and contents read and written through the fs plugin, and files dropped on the
window from the webview's drag and drop events, kept to those over the element.

The app registers `tauri-plugin-dialog` and `tauri-plugin-fs` and grants
`dialog:allow-open`, `dialog:allow-save`, `fs:allow-stat`, `fs:allow-read-file` and
`fs:allow-write-file`; both plugins add the chosen and dropped paths to the fs scope, so
no wider scope is needed. The suggested save location is the downloads directory.

Downloads.doc: Saves bytes as a file on the device: a download in a browser, the "Save as" dialog in Tauri.

FileDropZone.doc:
A dashed box that opens the file chooser when activated and receives files dragged onto
it from the desktop.

The chosen or dropped files go to `onFiles` unchecked; a `FileUploadController` checks
them against its limits. `accept` filters the file chooser. Drops pass every dropped file
even when `multiple` is off.

props.name: onFiles
props.doc: Receives the chosen or dropped files.

props.name: accept
props.doc: The file types the file chooser offers; empty offers every file.

props.name: multiple
props.doc: Whether several files can be chosen at once. Defaults to true.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether the zone opens the chooser and receives drops. Defaults to true.

props.name: hint
props.doc: A line under the title, such as the accepted types and sizes.

props.name: adapter
props.doc: How the zone reaches the platform; defaults to `defaultFilesAdapter()`.

props.name: minHeight
props.doc: The smallest height in pixels. Defaults to 160.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

FileUpload.doc:
A file upload: a `FileDropZone` that adds files to `controller`, the files refused by the
last addition with the reasons, and the list of accepted files with their size, a
preview of images and a remove button.

The zone hint defaults to the accepted types and the size limit of the controller; the
zone is disabled once the controller holds its largest number of files.

props.name: controller
props.doc: The controller that holds the files and checks their limits.

props.name: hint
props.doc: Replaces the default zone hint, which lists the accepted types and the size limit.

props.name: showPreviews
props.doc: Whether image files show a thumbnail. Defaults to true.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether files can be added and removed. Defaults to true.

props.name: adapter
props.doc: How the upload reaches the platform; defaults to `defaultFilesAdapter()`.

props.name: zoneMinHeight
props.doc: The smallest height of the drop zone in pixels. Defaults to 160.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The element.

DownloadTrigger.doc:
A button that saves a file built on demand with `Downloads`. A click awaits `data`, with a
spinner, and saves the bytes as `fileName`. `onSaved` reports whether the file was saved,
and `onError` receives a failure of `data` or of saving. Where files can't be saved, the
button is disabled and its tooltip says why.

props.name: fileName
props.doc: The suggested file name.

props.name: data
props.doc: Builds the file content when the button is activated.

props.name: mimeType
props.doc: The MIME type of the file; a generic binary file when left out.

props.name: children
props.doc: The button label; defaults to the localized "Download".

props.name: onSaved
props.doc: Called after a save with whether the file was saved.

props.name: onError
props.doc: Called when building or saving the file fails; the error is logged when it isn't set.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether the button can be activated. Defaults to true.

props.name: adapter
props.doc: How the button reaches the platform; defaults to `defaultFilesAdapter()`.

decorationMode.doc: Returns the decoration mode of the current window.

setDecorationMode.doc:
Applies `mode` to the current window through `tauri-plugin-oito2-window`. Call it
while the window is still hidden.

showWindowMenu.doc:
Shows the native window menu of the current window at `x`, `y` (CSS pixels from the
top left of the page), on Linux and Windows.

DecorationMode.doc:
How a window frame is drawn: the system frame (`native`), none at all
(`undecorated`, the app draws the title bar and resize handles), or GTK client-side
decorations with an empty title bar (`gtk-headerless`, Linux: GTK keeps the shadow and
resize edges).

NativeWindowController.doc:
Controls a Tauri window: minimize, maximize and restore, close, drag, resize and the
window menu, with a reactive `state` kept up to date from the window's resize, focus
and full-screen changes.

ResizeDirection.doc: An edge or corner of a window that resize handles drag.

initWindow.doc:
Prepares the current Tauri window and returns its controller for a `WindowScope`, or
`null` outside Tauri (in a browser), where title bars show no window controls.

WindowResizeHandles.doc:
Invisible handles along the edges and corners of an undecorated Linux window, which
resize it when dragged. They show only while the window has no system frame and isn't
maximized or full screen; GTK client-side decorations and the other platforms resize
the window themselves.

props.name: controller
props.doc: The window to resize; without one nothing renders.

props.name: thickness
props.doc: The thickness of the edge handles in pixels. Defaults to 6.

emptyRawSettings.doc: Settings with nothing read: no session, no keys, no files.

ConfigValues.doc: The values `tauri-plugin-oito2-settings` extracts from the desktop configuration files.

RawSettings.doc:
What `tauri-plugin-oito2-settings` reads from the platform: the session variables, the
GSettings keys (by `schema/key`), the configuration values and the toolkit's accent and
contrast. `composeSystemSettings` turns it into a `SystemSettings`.

SettingValue.doc: A GSettings value: a string or a boolean.

composeSystemSettings.doc:
Turns the values read from the platform into the `SystemSettings` of `platform`, with
the rules of `oito2_ui_settings`: the desktop environment from the session variables,
the button layout of each desktop's own settings (or its default), the accent and the
high-contrast preference. Outside native Linux only the accent and contrast count.

sameSystemSettings.doc: Whether two settings are the same, field by field.

settingsChangedEvent.doc: The event `tauri-plugin-oito2-settings` emits with the new values.

SettingsSource.doc: Where a settings scope reads the platform settings from.

loadSystemSettings.doc:
Reads the system settings once: from `tauri-plugin-oito2-settings` inside Tauri, or the
defaults of the platform in a browser or when reading fails.

SystemSettingsScope.doc:
Provides the real system settings to the components inside it, like `SystemScope`:
the desktop environment, the window control style and button layout, the accent color
and the high-contrast preference. It starts from `initialSettings` (or the platform
defaults), reads the settings through `tauri-plugin-oito2-settings` once mounted,
follows the changes the plugin reports (Linux) and reads them again whenever the window
regains focus (after the user changed them in the system settings). In a browser it
keeps the defaults.

props.name: initialSettings
props.doc: The settings before the first read. Defaults to the platform defaults.

props.name: source
props.doc: Where the settings come from. Defaults to the Tauri plugin inside Tauri.

props.name: platform
props.doc: The platform. Defaults to the running one.

props.name: onSettingsChange
props.doc: Called with the settings after each change.

props.name: children
props.doc: The content that reads the settings.

draculaPalettes.doc: The Dracula palette and its light variant, Alucard.

everforestPalettes.doc: The Everforest palettes, at the medium background contrast.

nordPalette.doc:
The Nord palette: Polar Night (`nord0`–`nord3`), Snow Storm (`nord4`–`nord6`), Frost
(`nord7`–`nord10`) and Aurora (`nord11`–`nord15`).

rosePinePalettes.doc: The Rosé Pine palettes: the main and Moon dark variants and the Dawn light variant.

DraculaPalette.doc: One Dracula palette: background, current line, text and accents.

EverforestPalette.doc: One Everforest palette: background layers from `bgDim` to `bg4`, text and accents.

RosePinePalette.doc: One Rosé Pine palette: base surfaces, text and the named accents.

presetColorTheme.doc: Returns the complete color theme of `preset`, raised to WCAG AAA with `highContrast`.

presetRoles.doc: Returns the role colors of `preset`, mapped from its theme family's palette.

presetTheme.doc:
Returns a theme source for `ThemeProvider`'s `light` or `dark` prop that builds
`preset` with the contrast the provider resolves.

themePresetNames.doc: The preset names, in display order.

themePresets.doc: The named presets, each with its display name and brightness.

ThemePreset.doc: The name of a preset, such as `catppuccinMocha`.
